IT’S FINALLY HERE… ❤️

Back-to-back Ironman race week.

I’ve said those words so many times over the last year, but it feels very different saying them now.

Because I can now say, this week I’ll stand on the start line of Ironman Kalmar 🇸🇪, complete 140.6 miles, travel to another country… then wake up the next morning and do it all again at Ironman Copenhagen 🇩🇰.

Am I nervous? Absolutely. 😬
Probably more nervous than I’ve ever been before a race.

But underneath those nerves, there’s also a strange sense of calm.

The training is done.
The long rides are done.
The endless swims, runs, early mornings, tired legs and moments of wondering “can I actually do this?” are done. I've put the work in.

Now there’s nothing left to prove in training. It’s time to trust my body, trust the process and do the thing I always tell my athletes and the most importantly — enjoy it.

Because however tough this weekend gets, I chose this challenge. I dreamed it up. And I know I’m incredibly lucky to get the chance to stand on those two start lines and raise money for the @ironmanfoundation 

So this week I’m going to try to soak up every single moment. The nerves. The excitement. The fear. The atmosphere. The finish lines.

All of it. ❤️

Back-to-back Ironman race week… let’s do this. 🏊‍♀️🚴‍♀️🏃‍♀️🔥

What does 2 Ironmans in 2 days actually look like in numbers? 🤯

I knew the weekend was going to be big but seeing it broken down like this makes it feel slightly ridiculous 😂

281.2 miles raced.
25 hours 38 minutes racing.
9,686 calories burned.
2,202m elevation.
Just 4.5 hours sleep between races.
And a 202-mile drive thrown in for good measure 🚗😅

But the stat that surprises me most?

Ironman number two was only 4.4% slower than number one. After everything my body had already done the day before, I still can’t quite believe that. It's a great reminder that your body can do more than you think.

And somehow, amongst all of it, Kalmar gave me a 52 minute Ironman PB ❤️

Numbers can tell you how far, how long and how hard but nothing will capture the incredible memories from that weekend that I'm so grateful for. One pretty unforgettable weekend. 🇸🇪🇩🇰

It was incredible to see what taking a step and then one more step led me to ❤️

————————————————————————————————Ironman rejsen blev til en personlig rejse.

“2026” blev året, hvor jeg ændrede stort. 

Jeg stoppede mit job. Købte lejlighed. Skiftede retning. Nogle kapitler blev afsluttet. Nye tog form.

Og midt i det hele kom skaden.

Hofte. Knæ. Astma.
6 måneder til Ironman.

Jeg var langt fra klar.
Men jeg måtte ikke stoppe.
Så jeg byggede mig selv op, indefra og ud.

Jeg læste. Reflekterede. Lærte. Voksede.
Trænede kroppen, men vigtigst af alt trænede jeg mit sind.

Ingen coach. Ingen klub. Ingen perfekt plan eller kost.

Bare disciplin. Konsistens. Tro.

I april kunne jeg løbe 5 km igen. 

Fem måneder senere gennemførte jeg Ironman Copenhagen. 226 km.

Men den største sejr er ikke medaljen.

Det er den person, jeg blev på vejen.

Jeg føler mig stærkere. 
I kroppen. I sindet. I min tro. Og i mig selv.

Og jeg er omgivet af mennesker og relationer, der føles ægte og rigtige. Kæmpe gave! 

For nogle gange skal man turde give slip på det gamle, før der bliver plads til noget bedre.

Og gennem hele rejsen havde jeg min tvillingebror, AMAN, med mig. ❤️

Når det blev hårdt, talte jeg til Gud.
Og til dig, min bror.

Dette løb var dit. Du gjorde det. Jeg fulgte bare med.

Taknemmelig for rejsen.
Taknemmelig for menneskene.
Taknemmelig for den, jeg er blevet.

Gud havde en plan hele tiden.
Jeg er kun lige begyndt. 🖤 #ironman #ironmancopenhagen

A week ago today, I took on my very first full-distance Ironman.

I’ve finally got the pictures downloaded, and going back through them has reminded me of just how much work went into getting to that start line in the first place.

I absolutely loved this race, and there were so many reasons why. My family and friends were there supporting me, my teammates were out there racing alongside me, and even those who couldn’t be there in person were watching from overseas and sending me messages that I got to read once it was all over.

I wasn’t sure how I’d feel at the end of such an epic day. Would I be part of the “one and done” crowd, or would I be completely hooked?

Well… I can assure you it’s definitely the latter! 😂

Thank you to everyone who supported me, believed in me and followed the journey. Every message, every bit of encouragement and every bit of support meant more than you probably realise.

It didn’t go unnoticed.

Here’s to the next one. ❤️

Much love x

I set myself two goals when I registered for Ironman Copenhagen back in August 2025. Looking back I’ve had a great build up through to some difficult training sessions and put myself into some really dark places in training. Training then over and Ironman Copenhagen itself was always about executing the plan. I’m over the moon with the result. The first goal was to complete in under 11 hours, the second to PB in the marathon. Admittedly, I had a fair bit of luck on the day, but I had prepared to push myself harder than I’d ever done before. I’ve shared my goals with friends and family and they’ve all offered amazing support and advice that I’ve taken on board, when the times got hard I thought back to those that had helped make this possible remembered the ones that are no longer here. Tan, you’ve been my biggest supporter and I couldn’t have done this without you.  In our own heads, if the ‘why’ is strong enough, then the ‘how’ is easy. Thank you everyone. Finally, Denmark, 🇩🇰 you’ve been everything I could’ve hoped for and more. #imcopenhagen #IronmanCopenhagen #IronmanCopenhagen2026

Ironman Copenhagen 2026 Debrief:

A tough day out. So pleased to finish another Ironman. The day didn’t go to plan, but that is part of this crazy sport. Still did a great time (10hrs38min), enjoyed a lot of it and put too much pressure on myself for some of it.

This is the celebration of the sacrifices, the long hours training and every high and low of the last 12 months. This hasn’t been an easy training year with illness, work travel and everything else in the mix, but we showed up and got it done.

Thank you to everything who has supported this journey. Forever thankful for my coach @stephclutterbuck, my physio @physiorun and my friends and family.

Huge shout out to @thetriguys_coaching who showed up en masse as athletes (62 competing) and all the support on course. Topped off by coming top tri club!

#ironman #ironmandenmark #triathlon

The top highlight of the day (1hr12min), a small but significant PB in the swim. Really struggled this year getting back into swimming after illness and my confidence took a huge hit.

Swimming is where I want to put a lot of focus going forward finding more flow and speed.

💜 FROM 5K TO IRONMAN — MEET THE IRREPRESSIBLE @yoga.with.diane 💪🏻🏊🏻‍♀️🚴🏻‍♀️🏃🏻‍♀️

When Diane first came to Fusion Endurance, she’d signed up for the Great North Run despite never having run further than 5K.

Fast forward a few years, a couple of 70.3 finishes, and one ambitious message to her coach…

“I’ve been thinking…” 👀😂

We knew exactly what was coming!

Ironman Copenhagen was booked, the training plan was in place, and another adventure was underway.

Was there self-doubt? Absolutely. Were there challenges along the way? Of course.

But with consistency, determination, a little reassurance, a little white lie about hills and plenty of laughs, Diane made it to that finish line.

And in her own words…

“WE GOT THERE AND HAD THE BEST DAY EVER!” ❤️

That’s what coaching at Fusion Endurance is all about.

Not just training plans, numbers and finish times. It’s about building confidence, overcoming doubts, adapting when life gets in the way, and helping ordinary people achieve extraordinary things.

Diane’s story is a wonderful reminder that you don’t have to be an Ironman to start. You just have to be willing to start.

The rest? We’ll figure that out together. 😉

Thank you, Diane, for the lovely words, the trust, and for reminding us why we love doing what we do!

FUSION ENDURANCE

Augustis võtsid WALLESSi tiimiliikmed Priit Raudsepp ja Andreas Veeret taas ette täispika IRONMANi – Priit Tallinnas ja Andreas Kopenhaagenis!

226-kilomeetrine katsumus koosneb 3,8 km ujumisest, 180 km rattasõidust ja täispikast maratonist. Kuigi distants oli mõlemale tuttav, kujunesid võistluspäevad väga erinevaks – Kopenhaagenis saatsid Andreast suurepärane atmosfäär ja hea ilm, Tallinnas tuli Priidul aga hakkama saada tugeva tuule, vihma ja külmaga.

Täispika IRONMANi läbimine nõuab järjepidevust, vastupidavust ja sihikindlust ka siis, kui finišijoon ei ole enam esimest korda tuttav. Palju õnne, Priit ja Andreas, järjekordse väga tugeva saavutuse puhul!
